Use a Tier 2 architectural change: add a jointly trained gated recent-item connection to the existing masked Transformer. The latest trial reached macro HR@10=0.5613, below the stated best of 0.5800, with Electronics remaining weakest at 0.4300. A plausible limitation is that the final mask representation dilutes the most recent interaction while aggregating the full history; relative position biases alone do not provide a direct path for that item’s identity.

Focus on model_design: concatenate each masked query’s Transformer representation with the embedding of its nearest preceding visible item, then use a learned vector gate and projection to produce one fused query representation. Score candidates using this fused query through the existing tied item embeddings and jointly trained item bias. For auxiliary masked positions, select the preceding item strictly from the corrupted input, excluding padding and mask tokens, so the connection cannot expose masked labels. Train this connection end to end within the same network, retaining the current sampled-softmax objective, sampling, optimizer, and hyperparameters to isolate the architectural effect.

In training_evaluation, compare the resulting macro HR@10 using the unchanged validation protocol and select exactly one checkpoint per category. Update the predictor writer to instantiate the gated architecture and apply identical sequence construction and fusion during validation and host inference. Preserve all four dataset routes, existing splits, seeds, and DATA_DIR handling; the host remains responsible for held-out evaluation. This experiment tests whether directly preserving recent-item information improves ranking while allowing the gate to retain broader context when the latest interaction is less informative.
